detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS with the modular input for `aws:s3:accesslogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.14.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `bucket` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:s3:accesslogs.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:s3:accesslogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:s3:accesslogs" key="us-only/*" | lookup geoip clientIP AS country | where country!="US"
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.14.29_object_storage_access_fr_29"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:s3:accesslogs` in `index=aws` to detect object storage access from geo-fenced prefix violation us. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon S3 console Server access logging for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `bucket` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_14_29_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
